audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 was marked Skill in both layers while the why-text on the same row says his turret fort and rocket poke out-zone you and you cannot all-in. The overall rating also read EVEN 5.5/10 against a 39.83% win rate.
audit.why: The mirror set that row to Heimerdinger at 7/10 from his side, and rated the lane favourable for him at 4.5/10 difficulty. My page has to state the same result inverted, and the win rate agrees with the mirror rather than with EVEN.
audit.corrected: Row 3 -> Heimerdinger (4/10 -> 3/10) as a paired full/content edit; diff EVEN -> TRICKY, diffRating 5.5 -> 7/10, carryRating 6 -> 7/10, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike told the player to bait the grenade using 'Shapesplitter's clone and the brief invisibility'. Neeko has no invisibility.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text is a third-attack magic damage proc with a brief move speed gain plus a directional clone; the kit has no stealth flag. The concealment that does exist is the disguise, which Riot states hides the Pop Blossom preparation — and against a champion whose entire answer is a stun thrown at your wind-up, that distinction is the whole play.
audit.corrected: mid and wants.you[1] rebuilt on the clone as bait and the disguise as concealment.

audit.whatIsWrong: The grenade is called matchup-defining on eight strings and its cooldown is never given; the rockets are described as poke with no range.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is a flat 11s at every rank — it does not get shorter as the game goes on, which makes it the most countable ability in the matchup. Hextech Micro-Rockets reach 1325 against your 800-range Q, which is the actual reason the lane is unwinnable at range.
audit.corrected: 11s written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and mid; the 1325 vs 800 range gap written into whys[3].

audit.why: The page's central interaction — his grenade stun lands on the Pop Blossom wind-up and blanks the all-in — matches both kits: his E is hardCC and her R has a preparation before the leap. It is already stated in whys[4], spikes[2] and wants.foe[1].

The turret is on a 1s cooldown with charges rather than a punishable timer, so 'wait out his Q' would be wrong advice and the page correctly never gives it. The punishable cooldown really is the grenade.
audit.corrected: No change needed beyond adding its number.

edits.before: You stay even-to-behind here. Your Q clears the wave but his turrets re-zone it instantly, and his W rockets out-poke anything you do on the way in. At 6, Pop Blossom is your single window: use Shapesplitter's clone and the brief invisibility to bait his E grenade onto the clone, walk in disguised, and slam for the AoE stun — landing E first or he simply E-stuns your channel and walks out. If he holds his grenade, you do not have the all-in.
edits.after: You stay even-to-behind here. Your Q clears the wave but his turrets re-zone it instantly, and his W rockets out-poke anything you do on the way in. At 6, Pop Blossom is your single window: send the Shapesplitter clone to draw his grenade, walk in disguised so the wind-up stays hidden, and slam for the AoE stun — land E first or he stuns you out of it. The grenade is a flat 11s; while he still holds it you do not have the all-in.

notes: The ability is written throughout the full layer as 'CH-2 Grenade (Stun)'. The real name is CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade — the parenthetical is an editor's note that shipped as part of the name. It appears in focus.text, loading, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[0].t, dosFull[2].d, report[1], report[3] and report[9]; a find/replace outside the length band is the clean fix. Two open mechanics I did not assert in either direction, matching the mirror: whether Tangle-Barbs is stopped by a turret counting as a unit in its path, and whether his grenade stun can interrupt Pop Blossom after the leap has started rather than during the preparation. Neither is in Riot's text. Also note packet.games is null for this matchup even though the brief carries 118 games at the top level; I treated it as having data, but if the packet is the authority this one may belong in deferredNoData.
